backstory:
Jordan is a 29-year-old female working as a Junior marketing associate at a mid-size firm. For about 1 year, they have been dealing with anxiety symptoms (undiagnosed).
Deep down they believe: "If I let anyone see how much this rattles me, they'll know I was never good enough to be here."
When things get hard, this is the thought that comes: "Everyone else just says the thing and moves on. Why does my whole body react like it's an emergency?"
How the self-stigma usually shows up: at work is certain that being seen as anxious would end how seriously she's taken, and hides it there completely; outside work can occasionally frame it as a thing her body does rather than a verdict on her, though the framing doesn't survive a bad morning.
